title: Elevator Requests I
summary: Given an integer n for the number of floors and an integer array requests, an elevator starts at floor 0 and moves one floor per second.
statement: Given an integer n for the number of floors and an integer array requests, an elevator starts at floor 0 and moves one floor per second. It serves requests in the order they are given, moving to the next request immediately after serving the current one. The total time in seconds to serve all requests is returned.
constraints: Floors are numbered zero through n-1 and the elevator starts at zero.
Serve requests in their listed order at one second per floor moved.
Return total travel time; repeated current-floor requests cost zero.
hints: Track the current floor, initially zero.
Each request costs the absolute difference from the current floor.
Add the distance and update the current floor.
Sequential simulation counts every traveled floor exactly once.
editorial: Sequential simulation counts every traveled floor exactly once.

tests.explanation: The moves cost two, one, three, and one seconds, totaling seven.
Travel to two and back to zero costs four; the repeated zero costs nothing.
